introduction: All 125 observations carrying our four project fields were re-reviewed, followed by a ring-boundary review of all 32 previously determinate ring labels. These examples use the latest decisions and show both category ranges and unresolved boundaries. “Pigment variation” is a visual score of photographed tissue; it does not measure chemical pigment.

traits.label: Petal Color
traits.summary: Judge the broad upper petal tissue between the veins. Exclude the yellow/orange throat, any separate white center ring, and the vein lines themselves. Our Figure 1 key is Pink A–F, Purple G–H, and White I–P.

categories.definition: White or near-white interveinal tissue, including a cool cast. Colored veins alone do not make a flower Pink or Purple.

examples.alt: An open white flower with very faint petal lines and a yellow-green center.
examples.title: White with very faint veins
examples.caption: The broad tissue is white and the fine lines are barely visible. Judge the petals outside the yellow throat.
examples.attribution: (c) Big Year, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC)
examples.cropNote: Cropped around the focal flower and resized for the scoring view; no color or contrast adjustment. Copied unchanged from the reviewed crop.

examples.alt: A cool near-white flower with faint veins.
examples.title: Cool near-white still counts as White
examples.caption: The tissue has a cool appearance but remains near-white. This project includes pale cool-looking flowers in White rather than treating every lilac cast as pigment.
examples.cropNote: Cropped around the focal flower and resized for the scoring view; no color or contrast adjustment. Copied unchanged from the reviewed crop.

examples.alt: A white flower crossed by a bold purple vein network.
examples.title: Purple lines, white background

examples.cropNote: Cropped around the focal flower and resized for the scoring view; no color or contrast adjustment. Copied unchanged from the reviewed crop.

examples.caption: The outer petal background is rose-pink. The diffuse pale inner area has no obvious outer edge, so its identity as a center ring versus broad pigment variation remains unresolved.

categories.definition: Clearly violet background tissue like G and H. The violet must be in the broad tissue, not confined to vein lines.

traits.label: Petal Vein Contrast
traits.summary: At the standard 300-pixel view, judge how strongly vein lines stand out from their immediate petal background. Assess prominence, not vein color, number, or branching.

categories.definition: Lines are faint, subtle, or not visible in an otherwise adequate image. Low does not mean veins are anatomically absent.

examples.alt: A sharply shown white flower with very faint vein lines.
examples.title: At the faint end
examples.caption: Fine lines are barely visible against the white tissue. The clear broad background supports Low rather than an uncertainty caused by blur.
examples.attribution: (c) Big Year, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC)
examples.cropNote: Cropped around the focal flower and resized for the scoring view; no color or contrast adjustment. Copied unchanged from the reviewed crop.

examples.alt: An ivory-white flower with pale subtle veins.
examples.title: Pale lines remain subtle
examples.caption: The pale vein lines are visible on close inspection but remain subtle at this standard size. They do not carry the readily visible contrast required for Medium.

examples.cropNote: Cropped around the focal flower and resized for the scoring view; no color or contrast adjustment. Copied unchanged from the reviewed crop.

examples.alt: A violet flower whose fine veins remain subtle against the colored tissue.
examples.title: Low on colored petals

examples.cropNote: Cropped around the focal flower and resized for the scoring view; no color or contrast adjustment. Copied unchanged from the reviewed crop.

examples.title: Visible pink lines on white

categories.definition: A strongly contrasting vein network is a dominant visual feature across the visible petals. Compare Figure 1 O and P.

examples.alt: A white flower with a dominant branching purple vein network.
examples.title: A dominant purple network

examples.alt: A white flower with bold contrasting colored vein lines across the petals.

categories.definition: Blur, inadequate source detail, glare, or clipped highlights prevent a reliable comparison between lines and background.

traits.label: White Center Ring
traits.summary: Inspect the transition immediately outside the yellow/orange throat on at least three visible petal bases. First decide whether a localized band can be separated from broad petal paling. Clear requires an obvious, traceable outer edge; diffuse paling alone does not establish a ring.

categories.definition: Colored petal tissue reaches the throat without an intervening pale or white band. The bases must be exposed well enough to establish absence.
categories.note: After the ring-boundary correction, none of the 125 reviewed observations remains a verified Absent example. Figure 1 D and F remain the reference definition. The two former photo examples are now Faint because a weak localized band is visible.

categories.definition: An actual weak, localized pale band is visible just outside the throat on at least three petal bases, but its outer edge blends softly into colored tissue. Faint is a visible band, not a substitute for uncertainty about diffuse paling.
categories.note: The first two examples are owner-corrected Faint anchors. A weak visible band rules out Absent even when its edge is too soft for Clear.

examples.alt: A violet flower with a weak localized pale circle around the yellow center.
examples.title: Owner’s anchor: a weak pale circle
examples.caption: A weak pale circle can be seen around the yellow center. Its presence rules out the earlier Absent label, while the softly defined outer boundary supports Faint.
examples.cropNote: Cropped around the focal flower and resized for the scoring view; no color or contrast adjustment. Copied unchanged from the reviewed crop.

examples.alt: A violet flower with a soft pale rim around the yellow-orange throat and broader modest petal paling.
examples.title: Owner’s anchor: a soft pale rim
examples.caption: The pale rim immediately around the yellow/orange center is visible but softly bounded. Score that localized band Faint; broader modest paling elsewhere in the petals remains Low variation.
examples.cropNote: Cropped around the focal flower and resized for the scoring view; no color or contrast adjustment. Copied unchanged from the reviewed crop.

examples.alt: A violet flower with a weak localized pale basal band blending softly into outer tissue.
examples.title: A weak, localized basal band
examples.caption: A weak pale band is localized immediately outside the throat, but blends softly into the surrounding violet tissue. The modest broad changes farther out are scored separately as Low variation.

categories.definition: A localized white band has an obvious outer edge that can be traced against the colored tissue on at least three visible petal bases. Width alone does not decide the category: a narrow band with an obvious edge can be Clear.
categories.note: Observation 77541853 is the project owner’s Clear anchor. Locate the outer edge of the band before choosing Clear.

examples.alt: A violet flower with an obvious white band and a traceable outer edge around the yellow throat.
examples.title: Owner’s anchor: obvious edges
examples.caption: An obvious white band surrounds the yellow throat. Its outer edge can be traced against violet tissue on at least three petal bases, establishing Clear.

examples.cropNote: Cropped around the focal flower and resized for the scoring view; no color or contrast adjustment. Copied unchanged from the reviewed crop.

examples.alt: A violet flower with a localized white basal band and a clearly traceable outer boundary.
examples.title: A defined edge against violet
examples.caption: The localized white band has a readily traceable outer edge against the saturated violet background on at least three petals. This edge separates a ring from diffuse inner paling.
examples.cropNote: Cropped around the focal flower and resized for the scoring view; no color or contrast adjustment. Copied unchanged from the reviewed crop.

examples.alt: A pink-lilac flower with a narrow white basal band and an obvious outer edge.
examples.title: A narrow band can be Clear

traits.label: Petal Pigment Variation
traits.summary: Look for repeated changes in pigment intensity within the broad background of a petal. Exclude the throat, narrow veins, a separately established center ring, shadows, glare, folds, and damage. If an ambiguous pale zone changes the score depending on whether it is included, use Cannot be determined.

categories.definition: The broad background is nearly uniform after the exclusions above. Both pale and deeply colored flowers can be None; a center ring alone does not increase variation.

examples.alt: A magenta flower with nearly uniform broad petal color.
examples.title: Nearly uniform pink
examples.caption: The broad pink tissue is nearly uniform. Folds and small flecks do not form a repeated broad pigment gradient.
examples.attribution: (c) Amy Frost-Wicks, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC)
examples.cropNote: Cropped around the focal flower and resized for the scoring view; no color or contrast adjustment. Copied unchanged from the reviewed crop.

examples.alt: A violet flower with uniform colored tissue outside a distinct white basal ring.
examples.title: Nearly uniform violet
examples.caption: The colored background is approximately uniform once the separate white basal ring is excluded. A ring is not a pale middle zone within the colored petal.
examples.cropNote: Cropped around the focal flower and resized for the scoring view; no color or contrast adjustment. Copied unchanged from the reviewed crop.

examples.alt: A white flower with approximately uniform tissue outside the yellow center and fine veins.
examples.title: Nearly uniform white

examples.attribution: (c) Big Year, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC)
examples.cropNote: Cropped around the focal flower and resized for the scoring view; no color or contrast adjustment. Copied unchanged from the reviewed crop.

categories.definition: A subtle but repeatable gradient or modest light/dark difference occurs across the broad tissue, without strongly separated pale and dark zones. An F-like near-white middle is not required.
categories.note: The first two photographs are the project owner’s Low anchors. Compare the broad tissue rather than only the flower’s overall hue.

examples.title: Owner’s anchor: paler middle regions
examples.caption: The project owner assigns Low here. Broad middle regions are paler than other petal regions beyond the narrow veins; the modest difference is enough even without sharply separated zones.
examples.cropNote: Cropped around the focal flower and resized for the scoring view; no color or contrast adjustment. Copied unchanged from the reviewed crop.

examples.attribution: (c) Trevor Van Loon, some rights reserved (CC BY)
examples.cropNote: Cropped around the focal flower and resized for the scoring view; no color or contrast adjustment. Copied unchanged from the reviewed crop.

examples.alt: A pink-lilac flower with modest broad petal variation beyond a clearly bounded narrow white center band.
examples.title: Modest variation beyond a clear band
examples.caption: The narrow center band has an obvious edge and can be excluded. Beyond it, modest broad lighter interiors and more pigmented outer regions repeat across the colored petals without F-like strongly separated zones.
examples.cropNote: Cropped around the focal flower and resized for the scoring view; no color or contrast adjustment. Copied unchanged from the reviewed crop.

categories.definition: Clearly distinct pale and dark broad background regions occur across the petals, as in Figure 1 F: pink toward the base, a nearly white middle, and deeper pink near the margins.
categories.note: No confident High example was found among the 125 reviewed observations. Figure 1 F remains the reference. Dark veins, stronger overall saturation, and a separate white center ring are not sufficient.

categories.definition: Use this when broad light/dark changes cannot be separated from illumination or image quality, when category boundaries remain unresolved, or when including versus excluding an ambiguous pale inner zone would change the score.

examples.title: Ring exclusion would change the score
examples.caption: The pale inner zone cannot confidently be separated into a center ring versus broad pigment variation. Excluding it would suggest a different score from including it, so None, Low, and High are all unsupported until that distinction is resolved.
